items.prompt: A gardener has 3/4 cup of soil and fills pots with 1/8 cup each. How many pots can be filled?
items.explanation: Rename 3/4 as 6/8, so six 1/8-cup pots can be filled.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: 4 is the 4 out of three-quarters, not a number of pots. Rename 3/4 as 6/8: six pots.
why.C: 8 is the 8 out of one-eighth. Count how many eighths are in 3/4: it is 6/8, so six.
why.D: 3 is the 3 out of three-quarters. As eighths that is 6/8, which fills six pots.

why.B: 4 is 10 − 6, the length minus the width. Divide instead: 180 ÷ 60 = 3.
why.D: 5 is 10 ÷ 2, half the length. The height is 180 ÷ 60 = 3.

items.subject: QR
items.prompt: A rectangle has area 54 square units and length 9. What is its perimeter?
items.explanation: Width=54÷9=6; perimeter=2(9+6)=30.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: 36 is 9 × 4, as if every side were 9. The width is 54 ÷ 9 = 6.
why.B: 24 is 9 + 9 + 3 + 3, going round a rectangle 9 by 3. This one is 9 by 6, because 54 ÷ 9 = 6.
why.D: 15 is 9 + 6, one length and one width. The perimeter is both pairs: 2 × 15 = 30.

items.prompt: A student doubles the number of pages read each week: 3, 6, 12, 24, ... . How many pages come next?
items.explanation: Each term doubles, so 24×2=48 pages.

why.A: 30 is 24 + 6, adding an earlier week on. The pattern doubles each time: 24 × 2 = 48.
why.B: 36 is 12 + 24, the last two weeks added. They double rather than add: 48.
why.C: 60 is 12 + 48, one week too many added on. Doubling 24 gives 48.

items.subject: QR
items.prompt: A supply count must be divisible by both 4 and 6. Which count works?

items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: 20 divides by 4 but not by 6. The count has to work for both: 24.
why.C: 18 divides by 6 but not by 4. The first that does both is 24.
why.D: 30 divides by 6 but not by 4. 24 divides by both: 24 ÷ 4 = 6 and 24 ÷ 6 = 4.
